1.source: Rewritten 2026-11-22 fresh from the public-domain King James Version, following the KJV's Greek text (Textus Receptus, checked against Moorman's 8,000 Differences). Checked against the full editorial guidelines: long KJV sentences broken into short ones, people named where a pronoun could be unclear, and hard KJV words kept and explained in parentheses every time.

verses.text: Paul, a prisoner of Jesus Christ, and Timothy our brother. We write to Philemon our beloved (dearly loved) friend, and fellowlabourer (fellow worker).
And to our beloved (dearly loved) Apphia, and Archippus our fellowsoldier. And to the church in your house:
Grace to you, and peace, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
I thank my God, making mention of you always in my prayers.
I hear of your love and faith, which you have toward the Lord Jesus. You have them toward all saints (holy people).
I pray that the communication (sharing) of your faith may become effectual (powerful). It becomes powerful by the acknowledging (knowing) of every good thing which is in you in Christ Jesus.
For we have great joy and consolation (comfort) in your love. For the bowels (deep love) of the saints (holy people) are refreshed by you, brother.
So I might be much bold in Christ to enjoin (command) you what is convenient (right).
Yet for love's sake I rather beseech (beg) you. I am such a one as Paul the aged. I am now also a prisoner of Jesus Christ.
I beseech (beg) you for my son Onesimus. I have begotten (become the father of) him in my bonds (chains).
In time past he was unprofitable (useless) to you. But now he is profitable (useful) to you and to me.
I have sent him again. You therefore receive him, that is, my own bowels (deep love).
I wanted to keep him with me. Then in your stead (place) he might have ministered (served) to me. I am in the bonds (chains) of the gospel (good news).
But without your mind (agreement) I would do nothing. Your benefit (good deed) should not be as of necessity (forced), but willingly.
For perhaps he therefore departed for a season (a while). Then you could receive him for ever.

Receive him not now as a servant, but above a servant, a brother beloved (dearly loved). Onesimus is beloved (dearly loved) specially to me. But how much more to you, both in the flesh (as a man), and in the Lord?
If you count me therefore a partner, receive him as myself.
If he has wronged you, or owes you anything, put that on my account.
I Paul have written it with my own hand. I will repay it. But I do not say to you how you owe me even your own self besides.
Yes, brother, let me have joy of you in the Lord. Refresh my bowels (deep love) in the Lord.
Having confidence in your obedience I wrote to you. I know that you will also do more than I say.
But also prepare me a lodging (place to stay). For I trust that through your prayers I will be given to you.
Epaphras, my fellowprisoner in Christ Jesus, salutes (greets) you.
So do Mark, Aristarchus, Demas, and Luke, my fellowlabourers (fellow workers).
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.
